Baboon killings in the Vineyards

By: Liz Fish | Production

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Gunshots and the sounds of screeching baboons had Constantia residents up in arms when they heard that two wine farms had been granted permits to shoot 2 baboons a day for a year. The SPCA says they were totally unaware the permit had been issued. Then 37 baboons were “missing” and all eyes were focused on the wine farms. They said they had only killed 7 baboons between the two farms and that it had been done by a professional hunter. They were quite within their legal right to do so, but baboons are such a sensitive topic in Cape Town. The City spends R12 million rand a year handling the baboon human conflict.

Summary:
The City has employed baboon watches who drive the baboons back from the urban edge into the Table Mountain National Park. The Park do nothing to keep the baboons within the Park because it’s an open Park. The vineyards are not on City property and so the Wine farms are left to their own devices. Over the years the Constantia baboon population has grown dramatically. There are over 400 baboons hanging out along 5 km stretch terrorising the farms daily. Instead of growing wine, the farmers are having to be baboon experts and are spending millions of rand trying to keep the baboons out. Buitenverwaght has spent R2 million just on the fence and have 3 men on bikes who parole all day plus the damages they have to repair. They are spending more money on baboon proofing their property than on employing a second teacher for the crèche.
Then after spending years sitting on the baboon Technical task Team and nothing was been done to assist them they learnt that as farmers they were within their rights to apply for a permit and so they did. If a raiding baboon was shot attacking a child or dog on the farm they would be in trouble so they applied and were awarded licences.



Further information:
Baboons would far rather raid the farms than forage in the fynbos. There is plenty of food on the mountains but raiding the wine farm is like going to Mac Donalds or KFC say the baboon ranger. They can get their calorie content within a quarter of the time. They could easily move back over the mountain but life is far easier in this small 5 km stretch. In the winter when the vines are brown then they hit the farm workers homes. Children can’t play outside. Dogs have been hospitalised with vet bills running into R25 000 for wine maker. The crèche children have been attacked for the piece of bread they were eating. Chicken coops have been raided. Pigs have died fighting with baboons which attack at night. Baboons are extremely clever and as soon as the rangers go home they descend. There are no natural predators left and the baboons know this. They even know when the rangers’ paintball guns are out of gas and will attack the rangers. Electric fences are only as good as their maintenance but porcupines dig under them, power supplies go down, rain washes out the fences and the baboons are back. On the Cape Flats it’s gang warfare here the raiding parties are baboons.
What most people don’t know is that wine farms in Franshoek only need a hunting licence and can shoot baboons anytime, and they do. They also don’t have a baboon problem because they shoot raiding baboons and they clear off. On avocado farms they don’t even need hunting licences and shoot or poison baboons. All food comes at a price to wildlife. Farmers around the country laugh at how much money the City of Cape Town spends keeping people and baboons apart. The Constantia wine farms are trapped in a PR nightmare, National Parks won’t help, the City drive the baboons out of suburbia and consequently they have been driven to above the wine farms and all they need is PETA to declare war on their wine like was seen with the Mohair farmers.
Buitenverwachting and Klein Contantia got a professional hunter to kill 7 problem baboons that were injured and they had identified as constant raiders. One injured baboon targeted the same home for 30 days in a row. The City has killed 70 problem baboons over the last 7 years. If a baboon targets an area it develops a “criminal record” and only then will it be eliminated. The only difference is that its trapped and injected which many argue is more traumatic for the baboon that just been shot by a hunter.
Only 7 were eliminated on the wine farms but activists like Baboon Matters have called for a boycott of their wine and a witch hunt to find the other baboons and are convinced there is a mass cover up. This kind of campaign makes good fund raising material for activist groups but researchers suspect that other people could have shot those baboons, some have point 22 bullets in them which professional hunters don’t use. There are also poor communities nearby that could hunt the baboons for bush meat. A baboon troop outside Kleinmond has entirely disappeared and it’s strongly suspected a nearby community from the DRC have hunted and eaten them.

Script:


Upsound from protest
Jenni “This professional hunting now is just completely unacceptable”
Script: Baboons are an emotionally charged topic in Cape Town, people were horrified when they heard that two Constantia wine farms had a permit to shoot two baboons a day. A professional hunter had shot 7. Baboon activists Jenny Trethowan says they didn’t know the rules had changed.
Jenny: “Right back in 1988 the baboon ordinance protected baboons from hunting on the peninsula, so as far as we were all concerned that ordinance still stood, so when they changed that ordinance nobody knows
Script: But to everyone’s surprise, including UCT baboon specialist Professor Justin O’ Riain, it turns out there is no such rule.
Justin ”The hunting season for baboons and other wildlife is closed on the peninsula…. This is an urban area it's not appropriate to be discharging guns in an urban environment and so that was the technicality.
Script: The farmers had tried everything imaginable, but the baboons were threatening their staff and animals. At a meeting at the end of last year, they discovered they could apply to Cape Nature for relief if they had tried all non-lethal methods. Cape Nature is the legal entity that issues the permits. Deon Hignett says they had done far more than most farmers.
Claire: Under what circumstances does Cape Nature issue permits?
Deon “If they can prove they have suffered damage, loss of crops, losses to infrastructure, time and effort to go and to manage the baboons. I think Buitenverwagting alone has spent five hundred thousand alone this year alone on baboon management.
Script: They are on the buffer zone between the National Park and the City, so they’ve been told to self-manage the baboons, explains Buitenverwagting owner Lars Maack
Lars “I took over from my family in 1990. I remember were about 30 baboons and they were very scarce. As soon as you walked up into those areas over here and they saw you they just ran they just disappeared.
Link: “There are 600 baboons across the Cape Peninsular but roughly 200 of them are concentrated here in this small area just above the Constantia wine farm
Justin “The density is extremely high probably the highest we know of in South Africa. So this is much higher growth than you would expect for a normal natural population. So we have two things at play here, we have a lack of predators, and we have a very abundant food source.
Script: Lars spends R50 000 rand a month managing baboons. The farms 3 baboon monitors have tried everything from leopard onesies to lion masks. The electric fences which were rebuilt after the 2015 fire, cost 2 million rand and needs constant maintenance. But no matter what they do, they’re under siege.
Claire “How dangerous are the Baboons.
Johannes “The other day. I was chasing them the whole day up and down and then I ran out of gas and they did attack me personally
Claire “They came for you.
Johannes” They came for me and then I started to ran
Script: Johannes Jansen is a diesel mechanic, but he’s been pulled out the workshop to chase baboons because the situation has got so out of control, and they still running circles around them.
Johannes “They do have electric fence. They take the shock if they want something there they they're going to get it. It's like when they sitting up there they look down into the farms it’s like your KFC your McDonald's everything is there that they want.
Link “These baboons are so smart they have adapted their behaviour they are like criminals they watch and time their break-ins they raid when the rangers knock off and a 7 foot electric fence is not enough of a deterrent to keep them out
Script Relda Budge who lives on the farm had an injured baboon raid her house every day for a month. They have broken into her home, and her kids are too scared to play outside
Reldha Budge “They hung on that door until the whole door broke off its hinges both doors was lying outside broken and then they got in and they destroyed the kitchen
Script: What shocks her, is the determination and the small spaces they manage to squeeze through
Reldha Budge “They literally stand and then they push their arm in and then the head goes in and then they in literally this size baboons will go into that little hole
Script: But poor Lexie, is taking the brunt of it
Reldha Budge “She had 2 major operations mauled at least 5 times and a few other times a swipe that we could treat at home she is full of scars …they had to do plastic surgery on her ear to stich it back.. 06 31 50 19 they also have bacteria in them so the infection rate is very high
Script: Baboons are not afraid of women, and they know the range of a paintball gun, so they and will sit just beyond its reach, and wait. There are 30 families that live on the farm, Aneesha Baartman runs the crèche and she fears for the children’s safety.
Aneesha Baartman “She was having a slice of bread and the baboon came jump over took the slice of bread and just ran off she was traumatised she was hysterical and I think it was a 3 year old.
Script: So now the children can’t eat outside, anymore.
Link “These baboons much like people have become addicted to sugar and rather than spending all day foraging for food in the mountains they would rather raid the wine farms for a quick fix
Script: And researchers have found, that the fat content of these male baboons, is far higher than normal. Right now, they are going for the cover crop, growing between the vines which doesn’t cause damage, but spring is just around the corner and they love vine buds which will wipe out the year’s crop
Johannes “One time we're fighting them over until nine o'clock at night. And I told my colleague, Guy I'm done I'm done with a day. It's become worse because the troops are increasing, its crazy.
Lars “So we used to have pigs on the farm. But then one night I heard the pigs just screaming squealing... The next morning we found out we saw that Baboon has attacked the pigs …[10:05:53] So they were opening up their teats and then trying to get the milk. Three Pigs died and we had to put down the other four pigs as well.
Script: The problem the farmers face is that nobody wants to take responsibility for the baboons. The City took SANPARKS to court and after a 5 year battle, they still couldn’t decide who the baboons belonged to. The Baboon Technical task team made up of The City, SANPARKS, Cape Nature and Table Mountain National Park meet regularly, but they all have different mandates.
Link “We wanted to talk to the baboon technical task team the overall body responsible for baboon management but we were told to speak to Brett Herron the mayoral committee member that’s an indication of just how sensitive this issue is
Script: The City is spends 12 million rand annually just keeping baboons out of the urban area.
Brett ”The history of baboon management is that almost nobody wants to take responsibility. So I mean the city has prepared some policy documents and some strategy document around baboon management. But the parties have been unable to agree to who is responsible for what.
Script But outside the peninsular, it’s open season on baboons. Justin says one farmer shot 500 baboons in a period of 3 years
Link “Wine farms outside the peninsular don’t have to apply for a special permit they can shoot two baboons a day all year round it’s a grim reminder that all food comes at a price to wild life
Justin “ That's the reality that the public doesn't seem to know and the protesters have to know it. But this is a far more convenient target. It's on the doorstep and it's highly visible that to be fair to baboons the real fight is out there it's not here.
Script: So because the City couldn’t help the farmers they got a permit from Cape Nature
Lars “ So we had one baboon who had a lame arm. We had one baboon that had a hand missing and then we had a third baboon with very bad burn wounds and was physically impaired. So those baboons struggle in the wild and then they are better off just raiding homes. And that's where they become dangerous. And in the meantime I have handed back my license because I want either the city or somebody else that operates for the city to handle those things.
Script: The City has euthanized 69 baboons in the last 6 years with a license from Cape Nature, did the farmers do anything different? They weren’t trying to reduce the population size, they were just taking out problem baboons.
Lars ”And I think that is maybe the biggest problem that there is no long term strategy. And what we're hoping for is that somebody will step in take leadership and just say this is the number of baboons that this terrain can handle.
Claire” Is the problem not going to escalate as there is less space for the baboons
Jenny “ If there was a proper management plan you would be looking at the carrying capacity you would be looking at the population ….look maybe the population is getting too big for the current availability and we need to start implementing things like birth control through contraception.
Script: But the City and UCT say there are 20 other baboons unaccounted for, Jenni and her informant were trying to find evidence of their remains.
Informant “There is a lot of baboons that have been killed they were killed at the bike trails plantation and their bodies were also buried there. It happened probably at night because when the rangers got there in the morning they found dead bodies of the baboons
Script: They found a site with the smell of dead animal, it could be a baboon, but it could also be a dead porcupine. There was also a pile of what looks like lime.
Jenni “ Nobody knows when baboons were killed or if indeed they are killed. One thought that's been put out was that perhaps they've moved and they're living happily in a valley that nobody's ever found and they are there
Justin “The farmers have gone to the authorities and applied for a legal permit. There's no reason to go and engage in illegal activity outside of the property that's carries serious reputational damage. I would say that's the first place I would look would be in residential areas that's the source of most of the illegal activity over the last decade.
Claire “There are baboons unaccounted are you doing anything to investigate this?
Deon “Without a doubt, if Cape Nature was presented with any evidence that a contravention of our ordinance was done , Cape Nature would definitely investigate any evidence that was presented to us without a doubt?
Script: But the troops are still massive, and invading daily, and with spring in the air, Johannes and his team will get very little rest till the end of April.
Johannes “They are like the skollies of the mountain even sometimes they take the electric shock as well just to get what they want

They have broken into her home, and her kids are too scared to play outside Reldha Budge “They hung on that door until the whole door broke off its hinges both doors was lying outside broken and then they got in and they destroyed the kitchen Script: What shocks her, is the determination and the small spaces they manage to squeeze through Reldha Budge “They literally stand and then they push their arm in and then the head goes in and then they in literally this size baboons will go into that little hole Script: But poor Lexie, is taking the brunt of it Reldha Budge “She had 2 major operations mauled at least 5 times and a few other times a swipe that we could treat at home she is full of scars …they had to do plastic surgery on her ear to stich it back.. 06 31 50 19 they also have bacteria in them so the infection rate is very high Script: Baboons are not afraid of women, and they know the range of a paintball gun, so they and will sit just beyond its reach, and wait. There are 30 families that live on the farm, Aneesha Baartman runs the crèche and she fears for the children’s safety. Aneesha Baartman “She was having a slice of bread and the baboon came jump over took the slice of bread and just ran off she was traumatised she was hysterical and I think it was a 3 year old. Script: So now the children can’t eat outside, anymore. Link “These baboons much like people have become addicted to sugar and rather than spending all day foraging for food in the mountains they would rather raid the wine farms for a quick fix Script: And researchers have found, that the fat content of these male baboons, is far higher than normal. Right now, they are going for the cover crop, growing between the vines which doesn’t cause damage, but spring is just around the corner and they love vine buds which will wipe out the year’s crop Johannes “One time we're fighting them over until nine o'clock at night. And I told my colleague, Guy I'm done I'm done with a day. It's become worse because the troops are increasing, its crazy. Lars “So we used to have pigs on the farm. But then one night I heard the pigs just screaming squealing... The next morning we found out we saw that Baboon has attacked the pigs …[10:05:53] So they were opening up their teats and then trying to get the milk. Three Pigs died and we had to put down the other four pigs as well. Script: The problem the farmers face is that nobody wants to take responsibility for the baboons. The City took SANPARKS to court and after a 5 year battle, they still couldn’t decide who the baboons belonged to. The Baboon Technical task team made up of The City, SANPARKS, Cape Nature and Table Mountain National Park meet regularly, but they all have different mandates. Link “We wanted to talk to the baboon technical task team the overall body responsible for baboon management but we were told to speak to Brett Herron the mayoral committee member that’s an indication of just how sensitive this issue is Script: The City is spends 12 million rand annually just keeping baboons out of the urban area. Brett ”The history of baboon management is that almost nobody wants to take responsibility. So I mean the city has prepared some policy documents and some strategy document around baboon management. But the parties have been unable to agree to who is responsible for what. Script But outside the peninsular, it’s open season on baboons. Justin says one farmer shot 500 baboons in a period of 3 years Link “Wine farms outside the peninsular don’t have to apply for a special permit they can shoot two baboons a day all year round it’s a grim reminder that all food comes at a price to wild life Justin “ That's the reality that the public doesn't seem to know and the protesters have to know it. But this is a far more convenient target. It's on the doorstep and it's highly visible that to be fair to baboons the real fight is out there it's not here. Script: So because the City couldn’t help the farmers they got a permit from Cape Nature Lars “ So we had one baboon who had a lame arm. We had one baboon that had a hand missing and then we had a third baboon with very bad burn wounds and was physically impaired. So those baboons struggle in the wild and then they are better off just raiding homes. And that's where they become dangerous. And in the meantime I have handed back my license because I want either the city or somebody else that operates for the city to handle those things. Script: The City has euthanized 69 baboons in the last 6 years with a license from Cape Nature, did the farmers do anything different? They weren’t trying to reduce the population size, they were just taking out problem baboons. Lars ”And I think that is maybe the biggest problem that there is no long term strategy. And what we're hoping for is that somebody will step in take leadership and just say this is the number of baboons that this terrain can handle. Claire” Is the problem not going to escalate as there is less space for the baboons Jenny “ If there was a proper management plan you would be looking at the carrying capacity you would be looking at the population ….look maybe the population is getting too big for the current availability and we need to start implementing things like birth control through contraception. Script: But the City and UCT say there are 20 other baboons unaccounted for, Jenni and her informant were trying to find evidence of their remains. Informant “There is a lot of baboons that have been killed they were killed at the bike trails plantation and their bodies were also buried there. It happened probably at night because when the rangers got there in the morning they found dead bodies of the baboons Script: They found a site with the smell of dead animal, it could be a baboon, but it could also be a dead porcupine. There was also a pile of what looks like lime. Jenni “ Nobody knows when baboons were killed or if indeed they are killed. One thought that's been put out was that perhaps they've moved and they're living happily in a valley that nobody's ever found and they are there Justin “The farmers have gone to the authorities and applied for a legal permit. There's no reason to go and engage in illegal activity outside of the property that's carries serious reputational damage. I would say that's the first place I would look would be in residential areas that's the source of most of the illegal activity over the last decade. Claire “There are baboons unaccounted are you doing anything to investigate this? Deon “Without a doubt, if Cape Nature was presented with any evidence that a contravention of our ordinance was done , Cape Nature would definitely investigate any evidence that was presented to us without a doubt? Script: But the troops are still massive, and invading daily, and with spring in the air, Johannes and his team will get very little rest till the end of April. Johannes “They are like the skollies of the mountain even sometimes they take the electric shock as well just to get what they want Invoicing Back references from Insert ID in Invoice: Title Author Last Updated Invoice for Baboon killings in the Vineyards (5293) lizfish@iafrica.com 31 August 2018

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Gunshots and the sounds of screeching baboons had Constantia residents up in arms when they heard that two wine farms had been granted permits to shoot 2 baboons a day for a year. The SPCA says they were totally unaware the permit had been issued. Then 37 baboons were “missing” and all eyes were focused on the wine farms. They said they had only killed 7 baboons between the two farms and that it had been done by a professional hunter. They were quite within their legal right to do so, but baboons are such a sensitive topic in Cape Town. The City spends R12 million rand a year handling the baboon human conflict.
metadata.Summary: The City has employed baboon watches who drive the baboons back from the urban edge into the Table Mountain National Park. The Park do nothing to keep the baboons within the Park because it’s an open Park. The vineyards are not on City property and so the Wine farms are left to their own devices. Over the years the Constantia baboon population has grown dramatically. There are over 400 baboons hanging out along 5 km stretch terrorising the farms daily. Instead of growing wine, the farmers are having to be baboon experts and are spending millions of rand trying to keep the baboons out. Buitenverwaght has spent R2 million just on the fence and have 3 men on bikes who parole all day plus the damages they have to repair. They are spending more money on baboon proofing their property than on employing a second teacher for the crèche. Then after spending years sitting on the baboon Technical task Team and nothing was been done to assist them they learnt that as farmers they were within their rights to apply for a permit and so they did. If a raiding baboon was shot attacking a child or dog on the farm they would be in trouble so they applied and were awarded licences.
metadata.Further information: Baboons would far rather raid the farms than forage in the fynbos. There is plenty of food on the mountains but raiding the wine farm is like going to Mac Donalds or KFC say the baboon ranger. They can get their calorie content within a quarter of the time. They could easily move back over the mountain but life is far easier in this small 5 km stretch. In the winter when the vines are brown then they hit the farm workers homes. Children can’t play outside. Dogs have been hospitalised with vet bills running into R25 000 for wine maker. The crèche children have been attacked for the piece of bread they were eating. Chicken coops have been raided. Pigs have died fighting with baboons which attack at night. Baboons are extremely clever and as soon as the rangers go home they descend. There are no natural predators left and the baboons know this. They even know when the rangers’ paintball guns are out of gas and will attack the rangers. Electric fences are only as good as their maintenance but porcupines dig under them, power supplies go down, rain washes out the fences and the baboons are back. On the Cape Flats it’s gang warfare here the raiding parties are baboons. What most people don’t know is that wine farms in Franshoek only need a hunting licence and can shoot baboons anytime, and they do. They also don’t have a baboon problem because they shoot raiding baboons and they clear off. On avocado farms they don’t even need hunting licences and shoot or poison baboons. All food comes at a price to wildlife. Farmers around the country laugh at how much money the City of Cape Town spends keeping people and baboons apart. The Constantia wine farms are trapped in a PR nightmare, National Parks won’t help, the City drive the baboons out of suburbia and consequently they have been driven to above the wine farms and all they need is PETA to declare war on their wine like was seen with the Mohair farmers. Buitenverwachting and Klein Contantia got a professional hunter to kill 7 problem baboons that were injured and they had identified as constant raiders. One injured baboon targeted the same home for 30 days in a row. The City has killed 70 problem baboons over the last 7 years. If a baboon targets an area it develops a “criminal record” and only then will it be eliminated. The only difference is that its trapped and injected which many argue is more traumatic for the baboon that just been shot by a hunter. Only 7 were eliminated on the wine farms but activists like Baboon Matters have called for a boycott of their wine and a witch hunt to find the other baboons and are convinced there is a mass cover up. This kind of campaign makes good fund raising material for activist groups but researchers suspect that other people could have shot those baboons, some have point 22 bullets in them which professional hunters don’t use. There are also poor communities nearby that could hunt the baboons for bush meat. A baboon troop outside Kleinmond has entirely disappeared and it’s strongly suspected a nearby community from the DRC have hunted and eaten them.
